title: Forgetting constant module coefficients compares derived restriction kernels
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in a common universe containing objects, arrows, covering index sets and coefficients [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a commutative unital ring, $A_{\mathcal C}$ its constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and $V:\operatorname{Mod}(A_{\mathcal C})\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ and $v:A\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}\to\operatorname{Ab}$ the scalar-forgetting functors [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a monomorphism $m:W\to T$ in $\mathcal C$, set
$$S_m^A(M)=\ker(M(T)\to M(W)),\qquad S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(G)=\ker(G(T)\to G(W)),$$
with restriction as the arrow and the induced maps on kernels as the functorial action. Both functors are additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Use bounded-below derived functors and integer cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories].

The category $\operatorname{Mod}(A_{\mathcal C})$ is abelian and has enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives]. If $I$ is an injective module sheaf [def-sp-injective-resolutions], its restriction $I(T)\to I(W)$ is surjective and $VI$ is $S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}$-acyclic, meaning $R^qS_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(VI)=0$ for every $q>0$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$c_m(K):vRS_m^A(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}RS_m^{\mathrm{ab}}(VK)$$
for $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Mod}(A_{\mathcal C}))$, normalized by the identity $vS_m^A=S_m^{\mathrm{ab}}V$ in degree zero.

More precisely, choose any bounded-below complex $L$ of injective module sheaves representing $K$, any bounded-below complex $J$ of injective abelian sheaves representing $VK$, and any quasi-isomorphism $q:VL\to J$ inducing these identifications. The maps
$$\ker(vL(T)\to vL(W))\xrightarrow{\ker(q)}\ker(J(T)\to J(W)),\quad q_T:vL(T)\to J(T),\quad q_W:vL(W)\to J(W)$$
form a morphism between the degreewise short exact restriction-kernel sequences. All three maps are quasi-isomorphisms. On derived objects the first is $c_m(K)$ and the last two are precisely the canonical ordinary evaluation comparisons of [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget]. These identifications are independent of $L,J,q$ and natural in $K$. No injectivity of $VL^r$ in abelian sheaves and no flatness of $A$ over $\mathbf Z$ is asserted.

proof.text: Evaluation is additive and preserves finite limits. The induced kernel maps are additive by cancellation of the monic kernel inclusion. A cone into the kernel functor is a cone into the source evaluation whose composite with restriction is zero; the universal properties of the evaluation limit and the objectwise kernel construct its unique limit lift. This proves finite-limit preservation of both kernel functors. The exact forgetting functors already installed by the ordinary evaluation interface preserve these kernels, and cancellation of the target inclusion proves naturality of the canonical kernel comparison.

Apply the source-library small-site theorem SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian to the actual constant RingCat sheaf. The Mathlib Grothendieck-category enough-injectives instance gives enough injectives for module sheaves. Abelian sheaves have enough injectives by the existing small-site Mathlib instances.

Prove module-injective restriction surjectivity directly for the constant RingCat sheaf. The right adjoint of exact module sheafification takes an injective sheaf to an injective module presheaf. The free-module presheaf map induced by yoneda(m) is monic because postcomposition with m is injective and Finsupp.mapDomain preserves that injectivity. Extend the free-Yoneda morphism representing a section over W across this monomorphism; naturality evaluated at the identity generator gives its preimage over T. For abelian injectives, apply the existing injective_sheaf_mono_restriction theorem.

The source theorem injective_module_abelian_acyclic makes positive object cohomology of a forgotten module-injective zero. Transport across nonempty_cohomologyPresheafFunctor_eval_iso_rightDerived to obtain right acyclicity for evaluation at every object.

Apply rightDerived_injective_sequence to kernel inclusion and restriction, using abelian-injective restriction surjectivity and the universal kernel exactness. At a forgotten module-injective, rightDerived_zero_transformation and left exactness identify the zeroth derived restriction with the original surjective restriction. In the derived sequence, exactness and that surjectivity kill degree one of the kernel; evaluation acyclicity at T and W kills every higher degree. This is forgottenKernelAcyclic.

The underived kernel comparison is a natural isomorphism, the forgetting functors are exact, and forgotten module-injectives are kernel-acyclic. Apply isIso_rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange_of_rightAcyclic to obtain invertibility of the canonical comparison. Apply rightDerivedBaseChange_zero_unit objectwise for its degree-zero normalization.

For any supplied L,N,q, restriction surjectivity gives both degreewise short exact rows; kernel.lift_ι and restriction naturality give the two squares. Source terms VL are acyclic for the abelian kernel and both evaluations; target terms are injective and thus acyclic. Choose the minimum of the two lower bounds and apply quasiIso_map_of_rightAcyclic to q for each of the three functors. Precomposition with the canonical termwise comparison isomorphisms gives the three asserted quasi-isomorphisms.

Evaluate rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange_fac on the homotopy class of L. Expand its associators and canonical composition comparisons; use full faithfulness of the inclusion of bounded-below complexes to identify the mapped underived comparison with the specified complexIdentity. Cancel the exact-forgetting factor isomorphisms. Naturality with eL, the supplied identification equation for q, and naturality of the target derived unit with q give comparisonCompute. Apply it first to the kernel identity and then to each evaluation identity. These are the specified representative equations, for every choice of representatives; the canonical natural transformation already ensures naturality and independence.
